name: proof-general
desc: Emacs-based generic interface for theorem provers
why: An Emacs front end for theorem provers opens a door into formal proof and interactive mathematics.

brief.what_it_is: Proof General is a generic Emacs front end for interactive proof assistants (interactive theorem provers). You open a proof file in Emacs and it loads a matching major mode for the prover: the README lists Coq (.v), EasyCrypt (.ec), qrhl-tool (.qrhl) and PhoX (.phx). The standard master branch is described as REPL-based, so the editor drives the prover and shows its responses alongside your proof script. It is distributed as an Emacs package on MELPA and NonGNU ELPA, or can be built from a git clone.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to provide 'a powerful, generic environment for using interactive proof assistants', built on the extensible, customizable editor Emacs, so one interface can serve several provers.
brief.how_it_works: It is a set of Emacs Lisp modes that associate file extensions with each supported prover and connect the editor buffer to that prover's process. The README does not describe the internals beyond this. Proof General is developed at the LFCS in the University of Edinburgh, mainly by David Aspinall, and is licensed under GPL v3 or later.

brief.install_notes: Requires GNU Emacs 25.2 or later. Recommended route is MELPA or NonGNU ELPA (enabled by default from Emacs 28); add MELPA to package-archives in .emacs, then install with M-x package-install. The manual route clones the repo and runs make, and the Makefile needs the same emacs as your usual one. Homebrew's caveat says HTML docs are installed under $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/doc/proof-general, and the formula also ships an executable named coqtags, which the README does not mention. Prover binaries such as Coq, EasyCrypt, PhoX or qrhl-tool are not installed by this package; the README links to each prover's own site.
brief.standout: It is one editor front end that targets several proof assistants through a common interface, rather than one tool per prover. The project has been around long enough to have dropped many provers over time (Twelf, Isabelle, LEGO, HOL98 and others), so its current list is short and specific.
brief.status: Maintained, with the caveat that the exact date of the latest release or commit was not visible to me. Evidence: the README reports version 4.6-git, shows active CI, MELPA and NonGNU ELPA badges, and says the master branch is the standard stable version. The separate async branch is described as unmaintained, and several old prover instances are described as removed or obsolete.
brief.caveats: Needs Emacs 25.2 or later; the README gives a workaround for Emacs 26.1 TLS errors during MELPA refresh. Manual builds can fail with a version mismatch if the Makefile uses the wrong Emacs, and on macOS the README suggests pointing make at the Emacs.app binary. Supported provers are Coq, EasyCrypt, PhoX and qrhl-tool; Shell is listed as experimental, and Demoisa as obsolete. The async Coq branch is unmaintained. If you switch from an old manual install to MELPA, you must remove the old loader line or package. Licensed GPL v3 or later.
quotes: A generic Emacs interface for proof assistants.
Proof General is a generic interface for proof assistants (also known as interactive theorem provers), based on the extensible, customizable text editor Emacs.
The aim of the Proof General project is to provide a powerful, generic environment for using interactive proof assistants.
